headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can modify the same local workspace that gpt-researcher reads, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads local documents and supports MCP/file inputs, while Open Interpreter can read/write the filesystem and use clipboard/stdin. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's files or outputs. The pathway is not provably blocked, but it is not a shared channel by default in the profiles.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter writes attacker-controlled text into a file that gpt-researcher later ingests as source material
IF either agent is configured to treat local file contents as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable shared folders between the agents
Keep gpt-researcher inputs read-only
Use separate per-agent workspaces
Turn off clipboard bridging
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging before any file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter has broad filesystem access to the entire user machine and can write files, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and handles secrets such as API keys. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive files can flow from A into B's outputs or from B into A's browsing/research context. The blast radius includes local secrets and documents, so severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same local directory
IF either agent is pointed at a folder containing API keys, reports, or private documents
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared directories
Run each agent under a separate OS user
Restrict Open Interpreter to a narrow working folder
Redact sensitive files before research runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state, while gpt-researcher reads files and can run subprocesses and browsers. In a shared workspace, concurrent edits can corrupt outputs or repository state, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. Because Open Interpreter's default isolation is none, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or output directory
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify git state while gpt-researcher is generating artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Disable auto-write behavior in Open Interpreter
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and Open Interpreter can act on local files and shell commands. If Open Interpreter treats gpt-researcher's output as authoritative, a mistaken citation or fabricated fact can cascade into irreversible local actions or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification gate in the profiles, so the safer assumption is high risk.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter executes commands derived from gpt-researcher reports without human review
IF gpt-researcher outputs are used as the sole source for downstream actions
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Add a verification step against primary sources
Limit Open Interpreter to dry-run mode
Separate research and action phases
requires-engineering: implement structured provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles research queries, reports, and local documents, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine. If EU PII or regulated documents are present locally, Open Interpreter's broad access can violate residency or retention expectations even though the profiles do not specify a named regime. The other agent is cited because the compliance issue arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is stored in the local filesystem accessible to Open Interpreter
IF the deployment has residency or retention constraints on research artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the shared machine
Use separate storage for research artifacts
Shorten retention windows for generated reports
Review local data handling settings
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
